saints.name: The First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The nameless Christians of Rome who died in Nero's cruelty after the great fire, the first martyrs of the city…
biography: When fire ravaged Rome in the summer of 64, the Emperor Nero, to divert suspicion from himself, laid the blame on the Christians and unleashed a savage persecution. The historian Tacitus records that a great multitude were convicted and put to death with mockery — some sewn in the skins of beasts and torn by dogs, others crucified or burned as torches to light Nero's gardens.

These were the first martyrs of the Church of Rome, many of them converts of the Apostles themselves, and their witness preceded or accompanied the deaths of Peter and Paul. The Church keeps their memory on the day after the solemnity of the two great Apostles.
saints.knownFor: The protomartyrs of the Church of Rome under Nero.
